**Reading**: the JS parser stops immediately after a literal TAB inside a character class (`/[ \t`…) → the next byte is a real NEWLINE where the source had an escaped \n. Identical cut point across ALL widgets = the corruption is in the SHARED delivery path, not in any widget source: a double-unescape of escape sequences (\\n → real newline) somewhere in widget-source assembly/fetch (prime suspect: the multi-file widget assembly from #1207 / its catalog serialization; the widgets themselves — pomodoro, focus-timer, reminders — are catalog-fetched, not bundled).

**The signal existed and was missed**: nightly's macOS suite has had the 5-test js-apps cluster red since 10-01 (#1266 — open_app launcher, dynamic_message tiles, js_theme) — the same subsystem. The nightly-red filer being dead (#1267 N3) is why nobody noticed before TestFlight.

**Fix:**
1. Reproduce: eval any catalog widget (pomodoro/widget.js) through the release assembly path on a device/sim — assert the byte stream entering the JS engine round-trips (source → store → load → eval) with escape sequences intact.
2. Find the unescape layer (assembly concat / catalog JSON / Dart→JS string bridge), fix so \n/\t survive; add the corrupted fixture from the log as a regression fixture.
3. Verify against #1266's cluster — likely the same root; close both together if so.

## NEVER-AGAIN (the owner's directive)

- **NG1 — release-blocking widget smoke (small set, CATALOG-FETCHED — per owner)**: a CI leg that downloads 2-3 widgets FROM THE REAL WIDGETS CATALOG (the same delivery path that broke — fetch → assemble → eval), boots them in the real engine stack (flutter_js on a macOS runner, same as device), and asserts `uiTree set: true`. Pick the set to cover the assembly variants: one regex-heavy source (the \t/\n char-class case), one minimal widget, one multi-file widget (the #1207 path). Pin the catalog revision for determinism, with a nightly live-revision run catching catalog-side drift. A widget-eval failure blocks merge AND release. (Today this surface is only nightly-and-excluded — see #1267 N1.)
- **NG2 — the corrupted-source fixture becomes a permanent regression test**: eval of a widget containing regex literals with \t/\n char classes must succeed byte-identically.
- **NG3 — wire #1267 N3**: had the nightly-red filer been alive, #1266's red cluster would have stopped 1.0.512 from shipping dead widgets. State that dependency explicitly when fixing.

**Acceptance:**
- AC1: FULL platform matrix (owner directive — every platform): the smoke set boots (uiTree set) on iOS, Android, macOS, and web builds carrying the fix; the catalog-fetch smoke leg runs on each applicable CI shape.
- AC2: NG1 leg exists, is required for release workflows, and demonstrably fails on a synthetic source-corruption fixture.
- AC3: root-caused to the exact layer with the byte-level explanation in this issue; #1266 cross-checked (same root ⇒ close as duplicate-of-fix).

## PR Description

## gh-1272 — every JS widget dead: `Unterminated regular expression literal '/[ ⇥'`

### Root Cause
- The shared host bootstrap `_faBootstrapJs` in `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart` was declared as a **non-raw** Dart string (`'''`). The gh-1164 fingerprint block inside it embeds JS regex char classes (`/[ \t\r\n]+/g`) and `'\n'` string literals; Dart's escape processing converted those to **real TAB/CR/LF at compile time**.
- The runtime concatenates the bootstrap verbatim into the script handed to the JS engine (no re-escape anywhere in source → store → load → eval), so every widget eval hit a real newline inside a regex literal — byte-identical failure for all widgets, exactly matching the TestFlight log. This is also the root of gh-1266's red js-apps cluster (81 `test/apps` failures on the broken tree).
- The file was additionally corrupt at rest in the same block (lines 1027/1040): the whitespace-collapse replacement string lost its space and closing quote (`' '` → `'`).

### Fix
- `js_app_engine.dart`: `_faBootstrapJs` is now a raw string (`r'''`, no `$` interpolation inside) so `\t`/`\r`/`\n` reach the JS engine byte-identically; restored the corrupted `' '` replacement on both fingerprint-normalizer lines.

### Test Coverage
- RED first: real QuickJS engine boot of a regex-heavy widget (`/[ \t\n]+/` char class) failed with the ticket's signature (`uiTree set: false`); after the fix it evals and renders, asserting the regex matches byte-identically (gh-1272 NG2 fixture).
- New pure-Dart regression test asserts the bootstrap keeps escape sequences byte-identical and leaks no real TAB/CR (catches any future non-raw reintroduction).
- `test/apps`: **519 passed** (was 441 passed / 81 failed before the fix). The 3 remaining failures (2× `js_app_error_capture`, 1× `open_app_tool`) fail **identically on the pristine tree** — pre-existing Linux-bridge artifacts (`{id: …}` console wrapping breaks the `faAppError:` JSON parse; a binding-init issue), not regressions.
- `flutter analyze` clean; `dart format` applied; bridge-parity suite green (70 tests).

### Notes
- gh-1266 cross-check: same root — the fixed tree turns its whole red cluster green; the two issues should close together (AC3).
- NG1 (release-blocking catalog-fetched widget smoke leg) and NG3 (wire gh-1267 N3) are CI/infra workstreams not covered by this code fix; the regression tests here are the deterministic per-PR guard in the meantime.

## Description

**User report (owner, fa 1.0.512 / TestFlight build 205, iOS, 2026-10-05): НИ ОДИН ВИДЖЕТ НЕ ОТКРЫВАЕТСЯ.** App-log evidence — three different widgets fail byte-identically:

[apps] engine start: pomodoro/widget.js
[FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend] starting JavascriptCoreRuntime
[FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend] evaluating widget code...
[FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend] widget eval error: ERROR: Unterminated regular expression literal '/[ ⇥'
[FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend] widget code done, uiTree set: false
```
(same for focus-timer/widget.js, reminders/widget_tile.js — the full log: owner's clip_1791188587332.txt)

**Reading**: the JS parser stops immediately after a literal TAB inside a character class (`/[ \t`…) → the next byte is a real NEWLINE where the source had an escaped \n. Identical cut point across ALL widgets = the corruption is in the SHARED delivery path, not in any widget source: a double-unescape of escape sequences (\\n → real newline) somewhere in widget-source assembly/fetch (prime suspect: the multi-file widget assembly from #1207 / its catalog serialization; the widgets themselves — pomodoro, focus-timer, reminders — are catalog-fetched, not bundled).

**The signal existed and was missed**: nightly's macOS suite has had the 5-test js-apps cluster red since 10-01 (#1266 — open_app launcher, dynamic_message tiles, js_theme) — the same subsystem. The nightly-red filer being dead (#1267 N3) is why nobody noticed before TestFlight.

**Fix:**
1. Reproduce: eval any catalog widget (pomodoro/widget.js) through the release assembly path on a device/sim — assert the byte stream entering the JS engine round-trips (source → store → load → eval) with escape sequences intact.
2. Find the unescape layer (assembly concat / catalog JSON / Dart→JS string bridge), fix so \n/\t survive; add the corrupted fixture from the log as a regression fixture.
3. Verify against #1266's cluster — likely the same root; close both together if so.

## NEVER-AGAIN (the owner's directive)

- **NG1 — release-blocking widget smoke (small set, CATALOG-FETCHED — per owner)**: a CI leg that downloads 2-3 widgets FROM THE REAL WIDGETS CATALOG (the same delivery path that broke — fetch → assemble → eval), boots them in the real engine stack (flutter_js on a macOS runner, same as device), and asserts `uiTree set: true`. Pick the set to cover the assembly variants: one regex-heavy source (the \t/\n char-class case), one minimal widget, one multi-file widget (the #1207 path). Pin the catalog revision for determinism, with a nightly live-revision run catching catalog-side drift. A widget-eval failure blocks merge AND release. (Today this surface is only nightly-and-excluded — see #1267 N1.)
- **NG2 — the corrupted-source fixture becomes a permanent regression test**: eval of a widget containing regex literals with \t/\n char classes must succeed byte-identically.
- **NG3 — wire #1267 N3**: had the nightly-red filer been alive, #1266's red cluster would have stopped 1.0.512 from shipping dead widgets. State that dependency explicitly when fixing.

**Acceptance:**
- AC1: FULL platform matrix (owner directive — every platform): the smoke set boots (uiTree set) on iOS, Android, macOS, and web builds carrying the fix; the catalog-fetch smoke leg runs on each applicable CI shape.
- AC2: NG1 leg exists, is required for release workflows, and demonstrably fails on a synthetic source-corruption fixture.
- AC3: root-caused to the exact layer with the byte-level explanation in this issue; #1266 cross-checked (same root ⇒ close as duplicate-of-fix).

## PR Description

## gh-1272 — every JS widget dead: `Unterminated regular expression literal '/[ ⇥'`

### Root Cause
- The shared host bootstrap `_faBootstrapJs` in `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart` was declared as a **non-raw** Dart string (`'''`). The gh-1164 fingerprint block inside it embeds JS regex char classes (`/[ \t\r\n]+/g`) and `'\n'` string literals; Dart's escape processing converted those to **real TAB/CR/LF at compile time**.
- The runtime concatenates the bootstrap verbatim into the script handed to the JS engine (no re-escape anywhere in source → store → load → eval), so every widget eval hit a real newline inside a regex literal — byte-identical failure for all widgets, exactly matching the TestFlight log. This is also the root of gh-1266's red js-apps cluster (81 `test/apps` failures on the broken tree).
- The file was additionally corrupt at rest in the same block (lines 1027/1040): the whitespace-collapse replacement string lost its space and closing quote (`' '` → `'`).

### Fix
- `js_app_engine.dart`: `_faBootstrapJs` is now a raw string (`r'''`, no `$` interpolation inside) so `\t`/`\r`/`\n` reach the JS engine byte-identically; restored the corrupted `' '` replacement on both fingerprint-normalizer lines.

### Test Coverage
- RED first: real QuickJS engine boot of a regex-heavy widget (`/[ \t\n]+/` char class) failed with the ticket's signature (`uiTree set: false`); after the fix it evals and renders, asserting the regex matches byte-identically (gh-1272 NG2 fixture).
- New pure-Dart regression test asserts the bootstrap keeps escape sequences byte-identical and leaks no real TAB/CR (catches any future non-raw reintroduction).
- `test/apps`: **519 passed** (was 441 passed / 81 failed before the fix). The 3 remaining failures (2× `js_app_error_capture`, 1× `open_app_tool`) fail **identically on the pristine tree** — pre-existing Linux-bridge artifacts (`{id: …}` console wrapping breaks the `faAppError:` JSON parse; a binding-init issue), not regressions.
- `flutter analyze` clean; `dart format` applied; bridge-parity suite green (70 tests).

### Notes
- gh-1266 cross-check: same root — the fixed tree turns its whole red cluster green; the two issues should close together (AC3).
- NG1 (release-blocking catalog-fetched widget smoke leg) and NG3 (wire gh-1267 N3) are CI/infra workstreams not covered by this code fix; the regression tests here are the deterministic per-PR guard in the meantime.

## Description

**User report (owner, fa 1.0.512 / TestFlight build 205, iOS, 2026-10-05): НИ ОДИН ВИДЖЕТ НЕ ОТКРЫВАЕТСЯ.** App-log evidence — three different widgets fail byte-identically:

[FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend] evaluating widget code...

Identical cut point across ALL widgets = the corruption is in the SHARED delivery path, not in any widget source: a double-unescape of escape sequences (\\n → real newline) somewhere in widget-source assembly/fetch (prime suspect: the multi-file widget assembly from #1207 / its catalog serialization; the widgets themselves — pomodoro, focus-timer, reminders — are catalog-fetched, not bundled).

**The signal existed and was missed**: nightly's macOS suite has had the 5-test js-apps cluster red since 10-01 (#1266 — open_app launcher, dynamic_message tiles, js_theme) — the same subsystem. The nightly-red filer being dead (#1267 N3) is why nobody noticed before TestFlight.

**Fix:**
1. Reproduce: eval any catalog widget (pomodoro/widget.js) through the release assembly path on a device/sim — assert the byte stream entering the JS engine round-trips (source → store → load → eval) with escape sequences intact.
2. Find the unescape layer (assembly concat / catalog JSON / Dart→JS string bridge), fix so \n/\t survive; add the corrupted fixture from the log as a regression fixture.
3. Verify against #1266's cluster — likely the same root; close both together if so.

Pick the set to cover the assembly variants: one regex-heavy source (the \t/\n char-class case), one minimal widget, one multi-file widget (the #1207 path). Pin the catalog revision for determinism, with a nightly live-revision run catching catalog-side drift. A widget-eval failure blocks merge AND release. (Today this surface is only nightly-and-excluded — see #1267 N1.)
- **NG2 — the corrupted-source fixture becomes a permanent regression test**: eval of a widget containing regex literals with \t/\n char classes must succeed byte-identically.
- **NG3 — wire #1267 N3**: had the nightly-red filer been alive, #1266's red cluster would have stopped 1.0.512 from shipping dead widgets. State that dependency explicitly when fixing.

**Acceptance:**
- AC1: FULL platform matrix (owner directive — every platform): the smoke set boots (uiTree set) on iOS, Android, macOS, and web builds carrying the fix; the catalog-fetch smoke leg runs on each applicable CI shape.
- AC2: NG1 leg exists, is required for release workflows, and demonstrably fails on a synthetic source-corruption fixture.
- AC3: root-caused to the exact layer with the byte-level explanation in this issue; #1266 cross-checked (same root ⇒ close as duplicate-of-fix).

## PR Description

## gh-1272 — every JS widget dead: `Unterminated regular expression literal '/[ ⇥'`

### Root Cause
- The shared host bootstrap `_faBootstrapJs` in `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart` was declared as a **non-raw** Dart string (`'''`). The gh-1164 fingerprint block inside it embeds JS regex char classes (`/[ \t\r\n]+/g`) and `'\n'` string literals; Dart's escape processing converted those to **real TAB/CR/LF at compile time**.
- The runtime concatenates the bootstrap verbatim into the script handed to the JS engine (no re-escape anywhere in source → store → load → eval), so every widget eval hit a real newline inside a regex literal — byte-identical failure for all widgets, exactly matching the TestFlight log. This is also the root of gh-1266's red js-apps cluster (81 `test/apps` failures on the broken tree).
- The file was additionally corrupt at rest in the same block (lines 1027/1040): the whitespace-collapse replacement string lost its space and closing quote (`' '` → `'`).

### Fix
- `js_app_engine.dart`: `_faBootstrapJs` is now a raw string (`r'''`, no `$` interpolation inside) so `\t`/`\r`/`\n` reach the JS engine byte-identically; restored the corrupted `' '` replacement on both fingerprint-normalizer lines.

### Test Coverage
- RED first: real QuickJS engine boot of a regex-heavy widget (`/[ \t\n]+/` char class) failed with the ticket's signature (`uiTree set: false`); after the fix it evals and renders, asserting the regex matches byte-identically (gh-1272 NG2 fixture).
- New pure-Dart regression test asserts the bootstrap keeps escape sequences byte-identical and leaks no real TAB/CR (catches any future non-raw reintroduction).
- `test/apps`: **519 passed** (was 441 passed / 81 failed before the fix). The 3 remaining failures (2× `js_app_error_capture`, 1× `open_app_tool`) fail **identically on the pristine tree** — pre-existing Linux-bridge artifacts (`{id: …}` console wrapping breaks the `faAppError:` JSON parse; a binding-init issue), not regressions.
- `flutter analyze` clean; `dart format` applied; bridge-parity suite green (70 tests).

### Notes
- gh-1266 cross-check: same root — the fixed tree turns its whole red cluster green; the two issues should close together (AC3).
- NG1 (release-blocking catalog-fetched widget smoke leg) and NG3 (wire gh-1267 N3) are CI/infra workstreams not covered by this code fix; the regression tests here are the deterministic per-PR guard in the meantime.

## Description

**User report (owner, fa 1.0.512 / TestFlight build 205, iOS, 2026-10-05): НИ ОДИН ВИДЖЕТ НЕ ОТКРЫВАЕТСЯ.** App-log evidence — three different widgets fail byte-identically:

[apps] engine start: pomodoro/widget.js
[FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend] starting JavascriptCoreRuntime
[FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend] evaluating widget code...
[FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend] widget eval error: ERROR: Unterminated regular expression literal '/[ ⇥'

(same for focus-timer/widget.js, reminders/widget_tile.js — the full log: owner's clip_1791188587332.txt)

**Reading**: the JS parser stops immediately after a literal TAB inside a character class (`/[ \t`…) → the next byte is a real NEWLINE where the source had an escaped \n. Identical cut point across ALL widgets = the corruption is in the SHARED delivery path, not in any widget source: a double-unescape of escape sequences (\\n → real newline) somewhere in widget-source assembly/fetch (prime suspect: the multi-file widget assembly from #1207 / its catalog serialization; the widgets themselves — pomodoro, focus-timer, reminders — are catalog-fetched, not bundled).

**The signal existed and was missed**: nightly's macOS suite has had the 5-test js-apps cluster red since 10-01 (#1266 — open_app launcher, dynamic_message tiles, js_theme) — the same subsystem. The nightly-red filer being dead (#1267 N3) is why nobody noticed before TestFlight.

**Fix:**
1. Reproduce: eval any catalog widget (pomodoro/widget.js) through the release assembly path on a device/sim — assert the byte stream entering the JS engine round-trips (source → store → load → eval) with escape sequences intact.
2. Find the unescape layer (assembly concat / catalog JSON / Dart→JS string bridge), fix so \n/\t survive; add the corrupted fixture from the log as a regression fixture.
3. Verify against #1266's cluster — likely the same root; close both together if so.

## NEVER-AGAIN (the owner's directive)

- **NG1 — release-blocking widget smoke (small set, CATALOG-FETCHED — per owner)**: a CI leg that downloads 2-3 widgets FROM THE REAL WIDGETS CATALOG (the same delivery path that broke — fetch → assemble → eval), boots them in the real engine stack (flutter_js on a macOS runner, same as device), and asserts `uiTree set: true`. Pick the set to cover the assembly variants: one regex-heavy source (the \t/\n char-class case), one minimal widget, one multi-file widget (the #1207 path). Pin the catalog revision for determinism, with a nightly live-revision run catching catalog-side drift. A widget-eval failure blocks merge AND release. (Today this surface is only nightly-and-excluded — see #1267 N1.)
- **NG2 — the corrupted-source fixture becomes a permanent regression test**: eval of a widget containing regex literals with \t/\n char classes must succeed byte-identically.
- **NG3 — wire #1267 N3**: had the nightly-red filer been alive, #1266's red cluster would have stopped 1.0.512 from shipping dead widgets. State that dependency explicitly when fixing.

**Acceptance:**
- AC1: FULL platform matrix (owner directive — every platform): the smoke set boots (uiTree set) on iOS, Android, macOS, and web builds carrying the fix; the catalog-fetch smoke leg runs on each applicable CI shape.
- AC2: NG1 leg exists, is required for release workflows, and demonstrably fails on a synthetic source-corruption fixture.
- AC3: root-caused to the exact layer with the byte-level explanation in this issue; #1266 cross-checked (same root ⇒ close as duplicate-of-fix).

## gh-1272 — every JS widget dead: `Unterminated regular expression literal '/[ ⇥'`

### Root Cause
- The shared host bootstrap `_faBootstrapJs` in `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart` was declared as a **non-raw** Dart string (`'''`). The gh-1164 fingerprint block inside it embeds JS regex char classes (`/[ \t\r\n]+/g`) and `'\n'` string literals; Dart's escape processing converted those to **real TAB/CR/LF at compile time**.
- The runtime concatenates the bootstrap verbatim into the script handed to the JS engine (no re-escape anywhere in source → store → load → eval), so every widget eval hit a real newline inside a regex literal — byte-identical failure for all widgets, exactly matching the TestFlight log. This is also the root of gh-1266's red js-apps cluster (81 `test/apps` failures on the broken tree).
- The file was additionally corrupt at rest in the same block (lines 1027/1040): the whitespace-collapse replacement string lost its space and closing quote (`' '` → `'`).

### Fix
- `js_app_engine.dart`: `_faBootstrapJs` is now a raw string (`r'''`, no `$` interpolation inside) so `\t`/`\r`/`\n` reach the JS engine byte-identically; restored the corrupted `' '` replacement on both fingerprint-normalizer lines.

### Test Coverage
- RED first: real QuickJS engine boot of a regex-heavy widget (`/[ \t\n]+/` char class) failed with the ticket's signature (`uiTree set: false`); after the fix it evals and renders, asserting the regex matches byte-identically (gh-1272 NG2 fixture).
- New pure-Dart regression test asserts the bootstrap keeps escape sequences byte-identical and leaks no real TAB/CR (catches any future non-raw reintroduction).
- `test/apps`: **519 passed** (was 441 passed / 81 failed before the fix). The 3 remaining failures (2× `js_app_error_capture`, 1× `open_app_tool`) fail **identically on the pristine tree** — pre-existing Linux-bridge artifacts (`{id: …}` console wrapping breaks the `faAppError:` JSON parse; a binding-init issue), not regressions.
- `flutter analyze` clean; `dart format` applied; bridge-parity suite green (70 tests).

### Notes
- gh-1266 cross-check: same root — the fixed tree turns its whole red cluster green; the two issues should close together (AC3).
- NG1 (release-blocking catalog-fetched widget smoke leg) and NG3 (wire gh-1267 N3) are CI/infra workstreams not covered by this code fix; the regression tests here are the deterministic per-PR guard in the meantime.

## PR Description

## gh-1272 — every JS widget dead: `Unterminated regular expression literal '/[ ⇥'`

### Root Cause
- The shared host bootstrap `_faBootstrapJs` in `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart` was declared as a **non-raw** Dart string (`'''`). The gh-1164 fingerprint block inside it embeds JS regex char classes (`/[ \t\r\n]+/g`) and `'\n'` string literals; Dart's escape processing converted those to **real TAB/CR/LF at compile time**.
- The runtime concatenates the bootstrap verbatim into the script handed to the JS engine (no re-escape anywhere in source → store → load → eval), so every widget eval hit a real newline inside a regex literal — byte-identical failure for all widgets, exactly matching the TestFlight log. This is also the root of gh-1266's red js-apps cluster (81 `test/apps` failures on the broken tree).
- The file was additionally corrupt at rest in the same block (lines 1027/1040): the whitespace-collapse replacement string lost its space and closing quote (`' '` → `'`).

### Fix
- `js_app_engine.dart`: `_faBootstrapJs` is now a raw string (`r'''`, no `$` interpolation inside) so `\t`/`\r`/`\n` reach the JS engine byte-identically; restored the corrupted `' '` replacement on both fingerprint-normalizer lines.

### Test Coverage
- RED first: real QuickJS engine boot of a regex-heavy widget (`/[ \t\n]+/` char class) failed with the ticket's signature (`uiTree set: false`); after the fix it evals and renders, asserting the regex matches byte-identically (gh-1272 NG2 fixture).
- New pure-Dart regression test asserts the bootstrap keeps escape sequences byte-identical and leaks no real TAB/CR (catches any future non-raw reintroduction).
- `test/apps`: **519 passed** (was 441 passed / 81 failed before the fix). The 3 remaining failures (2× `js_app_error_capture`, 1× `open_app_tool`) fail **identically on the pristine tree** — pre-existing Linux-bridge artifacts (`{id: …}` console wrapping breaks the `faAppError:` JSON parse; a binding-init issue), not regressions.
- `flutter analyze` clean; `dart format` applied; bridge-parity suite green (70 tests).

### Notes
- gh-1266 cross-check: same root — the fixed tree turns its whole red cluster green; the two issues should close together (AC3).
- NG1 (release-blocking catalog-fetched widget smoke leg) and NG3 (wire gh-1267 N3) are CI/infra workstreams not covered by this code fix; the regression tests here are the deterministic per-PR guard in the meantime.

# gh-1272: [BUG] [URGENT] 1.0.512 TestFlight (build 205): EVERY JS widget dead — engine eval error 'Unterminated regular expression literal /[ ⇥' on all widgets (source corruption in assembly/catalog path)

## Description

**User report (owner, fa 1.0.512 / TestFlight build 205, iOS, 2026-10-05): НИ ОДИН ВИДЖЕТ НЕ ОТКРЫВАЕТСЯ.** App-log evidence — three different widgets fail byte-identically:

```
[apps] engine start: pomodoro/widget.js
[FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend] starting JavascriptCoreRuntime
[FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend] evaluating widget code...
[FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend] widget eval error: ERROR: Unterminated regular expression literal '/[ ⇥'
[FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend] widget code done, uiTree set: false
```
(same for focus-timer/widget.js, reminders/widget_tile.js — the full log: owner's clip_1791188587332.txt)

**Reading**: the JS parser stops immediately after a literal TAB inside a character class (`/[ \t`…) → the next byte is a real NEWLINE where the source had an escaped \n. Identical cut point across ALL widgets = the corruption is in the SHARED delivery path, not in any widget source: a double-unescape of escape sequences (\\n → real newline) somewhere in widget-source assembly/fetch (prime suspect: the multi-file widget assembly from #1207 / its catalog serialization; the widgets themselves — pomodoro, focus-timer, reminders — are catalog-fetched, not bundled).

**The signal existed and was missed**: nightly's macOS suite has had the 5-test js-apps cluster red since 10-01 (#1266 — open_app launcher, dynamic_message tiles, js_theme) — the same subsystem. The nightly-red filer being dead (#1267 N3) is why nobody noticed before TestFlight.

**Fix:**
1. Reproduce: eval any catalog widget (pomodoro/widget.js) through the release assembly path on a device/sim — assert the byte stream entering the JS engine round-trips (source → store → load → eval) with escape sequences intact.
2. Find the unescape layer (assembly concat / catalog JSON / Dart→JS string bridge), fix so \n/\t survive; add the corrupted fixture from the log as a regression fixture.
3. Verify against #1266's cluster — likely the same root; close both together if so.

## gh-1272 — every JS widget dead: `Unterminated regular expression literal '/[ ⇥'`

### Root Cause
- The shared host bootstrap `_faBootstrapJs` in `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart` was declared as a **non-raw** Dart string (`'''`). The gh-1164 fingerprint block inside it embeds JS regex char classes (`/[ \t\r\n]+/g`) and `'\n'` string literals; Dart's escape processing converted those to **real TAB/CR/LF at compile time**.
- The runtime concatenates the bootstrap verbatim into the script handed to the JS engine (no re-escape anywhere in source → store → load → eval), so every widget eval hit a real newline inside a regex literal — byte-identical failure for all widgets, exactly matching the TestFlight log. This is also the root of gh-1266's red js-apps cluster (81 `test/apps` failures on the broken tree).
- The file was additionally corrupt at rest in the same block (lines 1027/1040): the whitespace-collapse replacement string lost its space and closing quote (`' '` → `'`).

### Fix
- `js_app_engine.dart`: `_faBootstrapJs` is now a raw string (`r'''`, no `$` interpolation inside) so `\t`/`\r`/`\n` reach the JS engine byte-identically; restored the corrupted `' '` replacement on both fingerprint-normalizer lines.

### Test Coverage
- RED first: real QuickJS engine boot of a regex-heavy widget (`/[ \t\n]+/` char class) failed with the ticket's signature (`uiTree set: false`); after the fix it evals and renders, asserting the regex matches byte-identically (gh-1272 NG2 fixture).
- New pure-Dart regression test asserts the bootstrap keeps escape sequences byte-identical and leaks no real TAB/CR (catches any future non-raw reintroduction).
- `test/apps`: **519 passed** (was 441 passed / 81 failed before the fix). The 3 remaining failures (2× `js_app_error_capture`, 1× `open_app_tool`) fail **identically on the pristine tree** — pre-existing Linux-bridge artifacts (`{id: …}` console wrapping breaks the `faAppError:` JSON parse; a binding-init issue), not regressions.
- `flutter analyze` clean; `dart format` applied; bridge-parity suite green (70 tests).

### Notes
- gh-1266 cross-check: same root — the fixed tree turns its whole red cluster green; the two issues should close together (AC3).
- NG1 (release-blocking catalog-fetched widget smoke leg) and NG3 (wire gh-1267 N3) are CI/infra workstreams not covered by this code fix; the regression tests here are the deterministic per-PR guard in the meantime.

1. Reproduce: eval any catalog widget (pomodoro/widget.js) through the release assembly path on a device/sim — assert the byte stream entering the JS engine round-trips (source → store → load → eval) with escape sequences intact.
2. Find the unescape layer (assembly concat / catalog JSON / Dart→JS string bridge), fix so \n/\t survive; add the corrupted fixture from the log as a regression fixture.
3. Verify against #1266's cluster — likely the same root; close both together if so.

- **NG1 — release-blocking widget smoke (small set, CATALOG-FETCHED — per owner)**: a CI leg that downloads 2-3 widgets FROM THE REAL WIDGETS CATALOG (the same delivery path that broke — fetch → assemble → eval), boots them in the real engine stack (flutter_js on a macOS runner, same as device), and asserts `uiTree set: true`. Pin the catalog revision for determinism, with a nightly live-revision run catching catalog-side drift. A widget-eval failure blocks merge AND release. (Today this surface is only nightly-and-excluded — see #1267 N1.)
- **NG2 — the corrupted-source fixture becomes a permanent regression test**: eval of a widget containing regex literals with \t/\n char classes must succeed byte-identically.
- **NG3 — wire #1267 N3**: had the nightly-red filer been alive, #1266's red cluster would have stopped 1.0.512 from shipping dead widgets. State that dependency explicitly when fixing.

**Acceptance:**
- AC1: FULL platform matrix (owner directive — every platform): the smoke set boots (uiTree set) on iOS, Android, macOS, and web builds carrying the fix; the catalog-fetch smoke leg runs on each applicable CI shape.

## Automated Code Review — APPROVE

**Summary**: Correct, well-tested root-cause fix for gh-1272. `_faBootstrapJs` as a raw string is verified safe (no `$` interpolation anywhere in the block), both corrupted fingerprint-normalizer lines are restored to `' '`, and the new byte-identity regression test plus the QuickJS round-trip test give strong never-again coverage for NG2. `flutter analyze` clean; the pure-Dart regression test passes locally (engine test skips on this host — no QuickJS bridge, as expected).

2. Track NG1 (release-blocking catalog-fetched widget smoke leg) and gh-1267 N3 (nightly-red filer) as follow-up issues; close gh-1266 with this fix per AC3 cross-check.

💡 **SUGGESTION: `isNot(contains('\r'))` may false-positive on CRLF checkouts**

The guard assumes the source file's line breaks never carry `\r`. If a contributor checks the repo out with `core.autocrlf=true` (Windows), the multiline raw string's own line endings could contain `\r` (depending on how the toolchain normalizes source line endings), making this assertion fail for reasons unrelated to the regression it guards. Two cheap hardenings, either is fine:

- assert only on the fingerprint-normalizer region (the substring between the first `__faFingerprint` and the closing of `__faReport`), or
- keep the whole-string assertion but document that the repo requires LF checkouts (e.g. a `.gitattributes` `* text=auto eol=lf` rule for `*.dart`) so the assumption is enforced rather than implicit.

Not blocking — current tree is LF-only (verified: zero TAB/CR bytes in the block) and CI shapes control their own checkouts.

## PR Description

## gh-1272 — every JS widget dead: `Unterminated regular expression literal '/[ ⇥'`

### Root Cause
- The shared host bootstrap `_faBootstrapJs` in `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart` was declared as a **non-raw** Dart string (`'''`). The gh-1164 fingerprint block inside it embeds JS regex char classes (`/[ \t\r\n]+/g`) and `'\n'` string literals; Dart's escape processing converted those to **real TAB/CR/LF at compile time**.
- The runtime concatenates the bootstrap verbatim into the script handed to the JS engine (no re-escape anywhere in source → store → load → eval), so every widget eval hit a real newline inside a regex literal — byte-identical failure for all widgets, exactly matching the TestFlight log. This is also the root of gh-1266's red js-apps cluster (81 `test/apps` failures on the broken tree).
- The file was additionally corrupt at rest in the same block (lines 1027/1040): the whitespace-collapse replacement string lost its space and closing quote (`' '` → `'`).

### Fix
- `js_app_engine.dart`: `_faBootstrapJs` is now a raw string (`r'''`, no `$` interpolation inside) so `\t`/`\r`/`\n` reach the JS engine byte-identically; restored the corrupted `' '` replacement on both fingerprint-normalizer lines.

### Test Coverage
- RED first: real QuickJS engine boot of a regex-heavy widget (`/[ \t\n]+/` char class) failed with the ticket's signature (`uiTree set: false`); after the fix it evals and renders, asserting the regex matches byte-identically (gh-1272 NG2 fixture).
- New pure-Dart regression test asserts the bootstrap keeps escape sequences byte-identical and leaks no real TAB/CR (catches any future non-raw reintroduction).
- `test/apps`: **519 passed** (was 441 passed / 81 failed before the fix). The 3 remaining failures (2× `js_app_error_capture`, 1× `open_app_tool`) fail **identically on the pristine tree** — pre-existing Linux-bridge artifacts (`{id: …}` console wrapping breaks the `faAppError:` JSON parse; a binding-init issue), not regressions.
- `flutter analyze` clean; `dart format` applied; bridge-parity suite green (70 tests).

### Notes
- gh-1266 cross-check: same root — the fixed tree turns its whole red cluster green; the two issues should close together (AC3).
- NG1 (release-blocking catalog-fetched widget smoke leg) and NG3 (wire gh-1267 N3) are CI/infra workstreams not covered by this code fix; the regression tests here are the deterministic per-PR guard in the meantime.

## Description

**User report (owner, fa 1.0.512 / TestFlight build 205, iOS, 2026-10-05): НИ ОДИН ВИДЖЕТ НЕ ОТКРЫВАЕТСЯ.** App-log evidence — three different widgets fail byte-identically:

Identical cut point across ALL widgets = the corruption is in the SHARED delivery path, not in any widget source: a double-unescape of escape sequences (\\n → real newline) somewhere in widget-source assembly/fetch (prime suspect: the multi-file widget assembly from #1207 / its catalog serialization; the widgets themselves — pomodoro, focus-timer, reminders — are catalog-fetched, not bundled).

**The signal existed and was missed**: nightly's macOS suite has had the 5-test js-apps cluster red since 10-01 (#1266 — open_app launcher, dynamic_message tiles, js_theme) — the same subsystem. The nightly-red filer being dead (#1267 N3) is why nobody noticed before TestFlight.

**Fix:**
1. Reproduce: eval any catalog widget (pomodoro/widget.js) through the release assembly path on a device/sim — assert the byte stream entering the JS engine round-trips (source → store → load → eval) with escape sequences intact.
2. Find the unescape layer (assembly concat / catalog JSON / Dart→JS string bridge), fix so \n/\t survive; add the corrupted fixture from the log as a regression fixture.
3. Verify against #1266's cluster — likely the same root; close both together if so.

## NEVER-AGAIN (the owner's directive)

- **NG1 — release-blocking widget smoke (small set, CATALOG-FETCHED — per owner)**: a CI leg that downloads 2-3 widgets FROM THE REAL WIDGETS CATALOG (the same delivery path that broke — fetch → assemble → eval), boots them in the real engine stack (flutter_js on a macOS runner, same as device), and asserts `uiTree set: true`. Pick the set to cover the assembly variants: one regex-heavy source (the \t/\n char-class case), one minimal widget, one multi-file widget (the #1207 path). Pin the catalog revision for determinism, with a nightly live-revision run catching catalog-side drift. A widget-eval failure blocks merge AND release. (Today this surface is only nightly-and-excluded — see #1267 N1.)
- **NG2 — the corrupted-source fixture becomes a permanent regression test**: eval of a widget containing regex literals with \t/\n char classes must succeed byte-identically.
- **NG3 — wire #1267 N3**: had the nightly-red filer been alive, #1266's red cluster would have stopped 1.0.512 from shipping dead widgets. State that dependency explicitly when fixing.

**Acceptance:**
- AC1: FULL platform matrix (owner directive — every platform): the smoke set boots (uiTree set) on iOS, Android, macOS, and web builds carrying the fix; the catalog-fetch smoke leg runs on each applicable CI shape.
- AC2: NG1 leg exists, is required for release workflows, and demonstrably fails on a synthetic source-corruption fixture.
- AC3: root-caused to the exact layer with the byte-level explanation in this issue; #1266 cross-checked (same root ⇒ close as duplicate-of-fix).

## PR Description

## gh-1272 — every JS widget dead: `Unterminated regular expression literal '/[ ⇥'`

### Root Cause
- The shared host bootstrap `_faBootstrapJs` in `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart` was declared as a **non-raw** Dart string (`'''`). The gh-1164 fingerprint block inside it embeds JS regex char classes (`/[ \t\r\n]+/g`) and `'\n'` string literals; Dart's escape processing converted those to **real TAB/CR/LF at compile time**.
- The runtime concatenates the bootstrap verbatim into the script handed to the JS engine (no re-escape anywhere in source → store → load → eval), so every widget eval hit a real newline inside a regex literal — byte-identical failure for all widgets, exactly matching the TestFlight log. This is also the root of gh-1266's red js-apps cluster (81 `test/apps` failures on the broken tree).
- The file was additionally corrupt at rest in the same block (lines 1027/1040): the whitespace-collapse replacement string lost its space and closing quote (`' '` → `'`).

### Fix
- `js_app_engine.dart`: `_faBootstrapJs` is now a raw string (`r'''`, no `$` interpolation inside) so `\t`/`\r`/`\n` reach the JS engine byte-identically; restored the corrupted `' '` replacement on both fingerprint-normalizer lines.

### Test Coverage
- RED first: real QuickJS engine boot of a regex-heavy widget (`/[ \t\n]+/` char class) failed with the ticket's signature (`uiTree set: false`); after the fix it evals and renders, asserting the regex matches byte-identically (gh-1272 NG2 fixture).
- New pure-Dart regression test asserts the bootstrap keeps escape sequences byte-identical and leaks no real TAB/CR (catches any future non-raw reintroduction).
- `test/apps`: **519 passed** (was 441 passed / 81 failed before the fix). The 3 remaining failures (2× `js_app_error_capture`, 1× `open_app_tool`) fail **identically on the pristine tree** — pre-existing Linux-bridge artifacts (`{id: …}` console wrapping breaks the `faAppError:` JSON parse; a binding-init issue), not regressions.
- `flutter analyze` clean; `dart format` applied; bridge-parity suite green (70 tests).

### Notes
- gh-1266 cross-check: same root — the fixed tree turns its whole red cluster green; the two issues should close together (AC3).
- NG1 (release-blocking catalog-fetched widget smoke leg) and NG3 (wire gh-1267 N3) are CI/infra workstreams not covered by this code fix; the regression tests here are the deterministic per-PR guard in the meantime.

**User report (owner, fa 1.0.512 / TestFlight build 205, iOS, 2026-10-05): НИ ОДИН ВИДЖЕТ НЕ ОТКРЫВАЕТСЯ.** App-log evidence — three different widgets fail byte-identically:

[apps] engine start: pomodoro/widget.js
[FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend] starting JavascriptCoreRuntime
[FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend] evaluating widget code...
[FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend] widget eval error: ERROR: Unterminated regular expression literal '/[ ⇥'
[FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend] widget code done, uiTree set: false
```
(same for focus-timer/widget.js, reminders/widget_tile.js — the full log: owner's clip_1791188587332.txt)

**Reading**: the JS parser stops immediately after a literal TAB inside a character class (`/[ \t`…) → the next byte is a real NEWLINE where the source had an escaped \n. **The signal existed and was missed**: nightly's macOS suite has had the 5-test js-apps cluster red since 10-01 (#1266 — open_app launcher, dynamic_message tiles, js_theme) — the same subsystem. The nightly-red filer being dead (#1267 N3) is why nobody noticed before TestFlight.

**Fix:**
1. Reproduce: eval any catalog widget (pomodoro/widget.js) through the release assembly path on a device/sim — assert the byte stream entering the JS engine round-trips (source → store → load → eval) with escape sequences intact.
2. Find the unescape layer (assembly concat / catalog JSON / Dart→JS string bridge), fix so \n/\t survive; add the corrupted fixture from the log as a regression fixture.
3. Verify against #1266's cluster — likely the same root; close both together if so.

- **NG1 — release-blocking widget smoke (small set, CATALOG-FETCHED — per owner)**: a CI leg that downloads 2-3 widgets FROM THE REAL WIDGETS CATALOG (the same delivery path that broke — fetch → assemble → eval), boots them in the real engine stack (flutter_js on a macOS runner, same as device), and asserts `uiTree set: true`. **Acceptance:**
